subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.

spec.name: Bauhaus Songbird on a Branch
spec.description: A life-size songbird perched on a gently curved branch, built from Bauhaus primary-colour geometry: a red sphere body, a yellow sphere head, blue half-disc wings, a black blade tail and a branch ringed in red, yellow and cream, with squares, circles and triangles for leaves.
spec.layout: Units are metres and the bird is life-size, about 0.25 m from beak tip (z +0.118) to tail tip (z -0.13). The branch runs along X (-0.25 to +0.25) and curves gently upward at both ends. Its lowest point, at x=0, rests on y=0 with axis y=0.02 and radius 0.02, so its top at x=0 is y=0.04. That top is the perch. The bird sits across the branch facing +Z, feet on the perch at x=±0.026. From the front the bird reads as stacked primitives. A big red ellipsoid body (about 0.055 half-width, 0.05 half-height, 0.075 half-length, centre [0,0.115,0.005]) carries a cream oval belly and a yellow triangle emblem on the breast. A black thin collar ring separates the body from a yellow sphere head (radius about 0.036, centre [0,0.165,0.062]). The head has big concentric-circle eyes (black, cream ring, yellow dot) at x=±0.027, a small red circular cheek disc under each eye, a red conical beak split into upper and lower jaw, and a crest of three flat triangles (red, blue, black) leaning back from the crown. The wings are folded on the flanks, angled slightly back and out, about 15 degrees off the body so they read as separate. Each is a blue half-disc or quarter-disc plate stack with a black bar, a cream stripe and a red triangle tip. The tail is a flat fan of three overlapping blocky rectangular blades in black, with a red centre stripe and a yellow tip square, sloping gently down and back from [0,0.108,-0.06] to [0,0.085,-0.13]. The thin black legs end in three forward toes and one back toe that wrap over the branch, with cream claw tips. The branch is charcoal, with alternating red, yellow and cream ring bands and two side twigs. One twig rises at x=-0.15 and carries leaves as flat blue squares, yellow discs and red triangles. The other twig points forward at x=+0.14. Every surface is a flat colour from the palette, and every motif (circle, triangle, square) is its own small part seated on the surface. Facets are visible (6 to 14 segments per primitive), nothing is smooth, and the layout is symmetric about x=0 except the branch twigs. Use primary colours for large areas and black, cream and charcoal for contrast; secondary hues are the only shading.

parts.builds: The red faceted ellipsoid body, a cream oval belly plate on the underside and chest, and a yellow triangle emblem seated on the breast. A blue half-disc rump patch sits at the lower back above the tail root. A black thin ring collar sits at the neck base [0,0.13,0.045], between body and head. A short yellow cylinder neck rises from the collar into the head. Add a black circle dot at the centre of the belly oval, and a row of three small cream squares down each flank under the wing root as Bauhaus trim. Everything is flat-coloured primitives (spheres, cylinders, extruded triangles, discs), 8 to 14 segments each. Wings, legs and tail attach to the body but are built by other parts. The body ellipsoid is about 0.055 half-width, 0.05 half-height and 0.075 half-length, centred at bodyCenter. It must leave room under it for the hips at y=0.085, and its lowest point stays above y=0.062.
parts.attaches: Neck cylinder top meets the head part at mount neckBase and headCenter. The wing parts start at wingRootL and wingRootR on the flanks. The tail part starts at tailRoot behind the rump patch. The leg part's hips at hipL and hipR sit just inside the lower belly.

parts.builds: The yellow faceted sphere head (radius about 0.036) centred on headCenter. Two big eyes at x=±0.027, y=0.172, z=0.08, each made of stacked flat discs facing outward and slightly forward: black outer disc, cream ring, black pupil and a small yellow dot. Each eye also has a thin black half-ring brow bar above it. Small red circular cheek discs sit below and behind each eye. The beak is two separate pieces: a red 4 to 6 sided cone for the upper beak from beakRoot [0,0.155,0.093] to a tip at z=0.118, and a smaller redDeep cone for the lower beak on the jaw joint, with a black thin line between them. A yellow-deep ring sits at the base of the beak and two tiny black nostril dots seat on the upper beak. A crest of three flat extruded triangles (red, blue, black, stacked and fanned slightly, with the tallest 0.03 high) leans back from the crown at crownTop. Add a small black circle on the forehead. Colours are flat; shapes stay low-poly. The head joint carries the head, the eyes and the upper beak, the jaw joint carries the lower beak, and the crest joint carries the three crest triangles.
parts.attaches: The base sinks into the torso's yellow neck cylinder at neckBase / headCenter. The crest sits on the crown at crownTop. The beak starts at beakRoot.

parts.builds: Two mirrored folded wings (left at +X, right at -X) that start at wingRootL and wingRootR and sweep back and slightly outward, about 15 degrees off the flank so they read as separate shapes. Each wing is a stack of flat extruded plates: a big blue half-disc or quarter-disc shoulder plate (thickness about 0.008), a blueDeep long blade extruded as a rounded rectangle for the flight feathers, running to the tip at wingTipL or wingTipR, a black bar across the middle, a cream stripe and a red triangle tip. Three flat feather blades of blue, blueDeep and black, fanned slightly, form the wing tip. A small yellow circle dot sits on the shoulder as an emblem. Outlines are bold and geometric, with each layer slightly offset outward so nothing is coplanar. Mirror with s=±1.
parts.attaches: The wing roots sit on the flank surface of the torso at wingRootL and wingRootR. The wings don't touch the tail but overlap it slightly at z about -0.08.

parts.builds: The tail and both legs with feet. The tail is three overlapping flat rectangular black blades fanned slightly, sloping from tailRoot [0,0.105,-0.06] to tip z=-0.13. A centre red stripe runs along the middle blade, with a yellow square at the tip and cream squares at the outer blade corners. It is built on the tail1 to tail3 joints. The legs are two thin black cylinders for the tarsus (radius about 0.004) from the hip at hipL/hipR down to the ankle, with a small redDeep feather-thigh sphere at the hip. Each foot has three forward toes and one back toe, which are thin black capsules (radius about 0.0035) wrapping over the branch top at y=0.04 (toe axes at y about 0.044). Each toe ends in a small cream cone claw. A tiny yellow sphere joint sits at each ankle. The toes rest on perchTop, with the left foot at x=+0.026 and the right at x=-0.026.
parts.attaches: The tail root begins at tailRoot at the torso's rear. The thigh spheres seat in the belly at hipL and hipR. The toes touch the branch top at footL and footR (y=0.04).

parts.builds: The charcoal branch, a swept tube along X from x=-0.25 to +0.25 with 6 to 8 sides. Its radius is 0.02 at the centre, tapering to about 0.013 at both ends. Its axis rises gently from y=0.02 at x=0 to y about 0.045 at both ends, so the lowest point at x=0 touches y=0 and the perch top at x=0 is y=0.04. Cut-end discs in cream cap each end. Flat ring bands (short wider cylinders) alternate red, yellow and cream along the branch at about every 0.05 m, skipping the perch zone |x|<0.04 so the feet are on plain charcoal. A twig rises from twigUpBase [-0.15,0.04,0] up and slightly back to about y=0.17, ringed with a yellow band. It carries Bauhaus leaves: a flat blue square, a yellow disc and a red triangle, each extruded 0.004 thick, sized 0.03 to 0.04, with a black circle dot in the centre of the disc. Another twig from twigForwardBase [0.14,0.04,0] points forward to z about +0.1 and slightly up. It has one red disc and one blue triangle leaf at its tip and a cream band. Add a tiny red sphere bud at each twig tip, plus a short stub twig stub on the back at x=0.2. The branch is the only prop; there is no base or ground, and the leaves stay above the wing height range and away from the bird, at x beyond ±0.1.
parts.attaches: The branch top at perchTop is the surface the feet touch. Everything here rides the root joint. Leaves and twigs stay clear of the bird's body and wings.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out the proportions for a Bauhaus-style songbird perched on a branch — a robin-like bird around 0.2 m long on a 0.5 m branch, with the branch resting on the floor so the lowest points touch y=0.

I'm working through the geometry: branch running along the x-axis with the bird facing +z, setting the branch radius and center height so its top surface sits around y=0.038, which becomes the contact point for the bird's feet, then stacking up the legs, body, and head from there.

For the design I'm leaning into Bauhaus colors — red, blue, yellow, black, and cream — mapping them onto the bird's parts: a red body, yellow head, blue wing, black tail blades with a colored stripe, a contrasting beak, concentric black-and-white eyes, and a black branch with geometric ring bands for visual rhythm.

Now I'm starting to lay out the skeleton/rig: defining the root body joint and spine chain, planning neck, head, jaw, tail segments, wing and leg joints with roles, and setting initial positions and directions for each.

Working out body proportions now: body centered around y 0.115 with radius ~0.05, head centered at [0,0.165,0.06] with radius 0.036 giving total height 0.2, and a tail chain sloping from the rear down to y 0.09 at the tip. Now I'm positioning the wing joints starting with wingL near the shoulder.

For the legs, I'm placing hipL and an ankleL joint representing the tarsus, then adding toe joints (front, in, out, back digits) positioned where the foot grips the branch top around y=0.04-0.045, with toes extending forward across the branch since it runs along x while toes wrap along z. I'm noting the convention that L-side joints get positive X.

Totaling things up: body, chest, neck, head, jaw, three tail segments, three wing joints per side, hip/ankle pairs, and three toes per foot gives roughly 25 joints overall, which seems like a reasonable count, and I'm considering whether to add a crest joint too.

Then I'm working through the root joint structure - deciding whether the perch/branch element needs its own joint or should just attach to the root, and settling on naming the root joint something like "root" with a spine role, positioned near the origin.

I'm now outlining how to split the bird's parts among five builders: one group handling the torso (body ellipsoid, belly, breast patch, back saddle, rump, neck collar, with body/chest/neck joints), and another handling the head (sphere shape plus beak).

Head group also covers eyes, cheeks, crest, and brow with their joints; wings group covers both wings and the geometric shoulder covering with blue/red/yellow accents and wing joints; and the tail-and-legs group covers tail feathers, legs, feet, and all their joints, leaving the branch as the fifth composition piece with its twigs, rings, leaves, and buds.

Now I'm pinning down exact coordinates for each mount point—neck base, head center, beak root, left/right wing roots, tail root, hip, perch top, and feet—to define how the body parts attach to each other and to the branch.

For the branch itself, I'm figuring out its shape: a slightly tapered tube running along the x-axis from -0.25 to 0.25, sitting the bird at the top center around y=0.04, and working out the radius profile so it tapers from about 0.02 at center to 0.013 at the tips while still touching the ground properly.

I'll give the branch a subtle upward curve with the center lowest, add two forking twigs with leaves (one going up-back on the left, one forward on the right), keep everything within a height limit of 0.2, and define the overall bounding size as [0.5, 0.2, 0.26]. Now I'm settling on a limited color palette of around two dozen colors for the whole piece.

I'm picking a Bauhaus-inspired scheme avoiding green, favoring red, blue, yellow, black, cream, and charcoal variants, and planning the bird's coloring: red body, cream belly, yellow head, blue wing with a black bar and cream accent, black tail with a red stripe, and a black beak against the yellow head.

I'm landing on the eye and beak details — a black disc eye with a cream ring and yellow dot, red cheek patch, and a red upper beak with a deeper red lower beak to contrast the yellow head — plus black legs and toes with cream claws, and now I'm starting to assemble the torso shape.

Still defining bounding boxes...

Continuing tail joints down to the tip, then placing hip, ankle, and toe joints for the leg so the foot grips the branch, with toes angled slightly forward and outward to wrap around the perch.

Moving to the neck and head: positioning the neck joint, head center, and jaw hinge, then working out the beak geometry so the upper mandible tip lines up correctly in front of the face.

Pinning down eye placement and the crest joint position and hinge direction, then I'll draft the full JSON spec -- noting conventions like left being +X, low-poly circles with 10-16 segments, flat colors, consistent scale, no underscores in names, and the root node at the base with its spine role.
